subject: Commercial close plan: MAP milestones, commit & latency SLO tie-ins
messages:
From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acme.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP & initial commercial asks

Rishi,

Thanks for the call earlier — Acme is aligned on a 12-week evaluation but we need a tighter commercial runway to hit exec approval. Attached is our suggested MAP (high level): discovery (weeks 1–2), evaluation automation (weeks 3–6), performance stress & security (weeks 7–9), close & procurement (weeks 10–12).

Key asks from my side: an initial committed capacity (reserved burst) to guarantee latency during the eval, and a discount corridor if we commit to a 12-month reserved plan within 30 days of a successful eval. Also, the procurement team wants SLO commitments for 95th p99 latency for the endpoints used in evaluation — they may want credits if we miss targets.

I attached a quick MAP template (MAP_v1_acme_redwood.xlsx) and the eval testset we plan to use (evaluation-plan-qa-set.csv). Can you confirm whether Redwood can tie discounts to milestone signoffs and define the SLO/credit table?

Claire
Claire Johnson
Head of ML Platforms, Acme AI
(attachment: MAP_v1_acme_redwood.xlsx (xlsx, 58KB))
(attachment: evaluation-plan-qa-set.csv (csv, 120KB))

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft MAP & initial commercial asks — need input on SLO-credit linkage

Team — forwarding Claire's MAP and asks. Short answers I need for tomorrow's sync with procurement: 1) Can we commit to reserved burst for the eval (short-lived reservation) and how do we price it? 2) Are we comfortable structuring a milestone discount that vests after a post-eval 12-month committed purchase? 3) What SLO thresholds are reasonable for credits (95th p99 numbers) given their testset?

Notes: Acme is a high strategic account; winning this could justify an initial market reference. I want pragmatic language that legal can bake into a simple LOI: tiered discounts based on execution of the MAP (e.g., 5% at formal acceptance, 10% after production ramp to commit levels). But procurement specifically asked if discounts can be conditional on SLOs — they will push for credit triggers.

Please reply inline.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP_v1_acme_redwood.xlsx)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2026 14:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft MAP & initial commercial asks — need input on SLO-credit linkage

Rishi — quick thoughts from product/serving runtime perspective:

- Reserved burst for eval: feasible as a short-term dedicated pool (2–4 weeks). Recommend flat fee for the reservation + usage. We can size based on the eval request; I'll ask infra for two sizing options (conservative / aggressive).

- Milestone discounts: OK to do staged discounts tied to MAP signoffs. Prefer time-boxed milestones with objective acceptance criteria (e.g., eval pass rate, latency on canonical workload).

- SLOs and credits: avoid dollar-for-dollar discounts linked to SLO breaches. Instead, propose a pre-defined service credit schedule tied to monthly P95/P99 latency windows. Example table in SLA_credit_table.pdf: if P99 > 500ms for >=2 production weeks during ramp => 5% service credit; P99 > 800ms => 10% credit. We can cap total credits per quarter and tie the ramp stages to credit exposure. That keeps our upside protected while giving Acme recourse.

I'll attach a proposed credit table and sample acceptance criteria. Priyom, can you draft the acceptance checklist for the MAP steps so legal has concrete pass/fail items?

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
(attachment: SLA_credit_table.pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & initial commercial asks

Claire — thanks, this is helpful. Attached is an updated MAP and an initial commercial proposal from our side. High-level summary:

- Eval plan: 12-week MAP as you outlined, with objective acceptance criteria per milestone (Priyom will include a checklist).
- Capacity: Redwood will provision a short-term reserved burst for the evaluation (2–6 weeks) at a fixed reservation fee; usage billed on top.
- Commit/discount: If Acme signs a 12-month reserved commitment within 30 days of a successful eval close, Redwood will apply staged discounts: 5% on initial order upon LOI, additional 5% after 3-month production ramp to commit levels.
- SLA / credits: Per Dev's attachment, we propose a bounded service-credit table tied to P95/P99 on the evaluation endpoints. Credits are limited per quarter and do not exceed X% of monthly recurring revenue for the committed plan.

I've attached: MAP_v1_acme_redwood.xlsx (updated), SLA_credit_table.pdf, and the eval testset reference. Also linking to our HubSpot deal for procurement. If this looks good I suggest a short LOI that references the MAP, attachments, and a statement that final commercial terms will be captured in the definitive agreement.

Next steps: Claire — are you comfortable with the credit caps and the 30-day commit trigger? If procurement wants different language (e.g., discount vesting tied strictly to SLOs rather than milestone signoff), flag the exact phrasing.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP_v1_acme_redwood.xlsx)
(attachment: SLA_credit_table.pdf)
(attachment: evaluation-plan-qa-set.csv)

From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acme.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme AI - Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & initial commercial asks

Rishi — thanks for the update and the proposed structure. Procurement reviewed and asked for two adjustments: 1) extend the commit window from 30 days to 60 days (procurement lead wants more time for legal/finance), and 2) increase the maximum service credit to cover up to two months of committed spend if SLOs are missed during the ramp — they argue ramp incidents are more impactful.

We are willing to accept the staged discount model, but procurement insists that at least one portion of the discount (the second 5%) should be explicitly tied to meeting the P99 threshold during the ramp month (i.e., a technical gate). They also asked for a short clause of make-good priority engineering support for the first 90 days of production.

Can Redwood confirm whether the 60-day commit window and the increased credit exposure (with an explicit P99 gate for the second discount tranche) are workable? If so, we can move to LOI and get procurement/legal involved.

On the MAP timeline: we might accelerate some evaluation steps depending on results; will that change the reserved burst pricing?

Claire
On Tue, Jun 8, 2026 at 09:12 AM -0700, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks — noted.
>
> —R

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & initial commercial asks — confirmation of concessions and next steps

Team/Claire — following up after procurement's message and our internal reviews:

- Commit window: we can extend the commit trigger to 60 days. Finance ok'd the shift given strategic value. We'll note this in the LOI.
- Credit exposure: we will accept an increased credit cap that can reach up to two months of committed monthly spend, but only if the customer's MAP acceptance checklist is followed and the ramp month is clearly defined in the LOI. Credits apply only to production endpoints defined in the checklist.
- P99 gate for second discount: we will agree to make the second 5% tranche contingent on meeting the P99 threshold during the defined ramp month. If the threshold is not met, that tranche will not vest; instead, service credits will apply per the SLA table.
- Make-good support: Redwood will provide priority engineering hours (up to 40 hours in the first 90 days) for ramp remediation. Any excess will be billed at standard SOW rates.
- Reserved burst pricing: if Acme accelerates the MAP and reduces reservation length, we'll pro-rate the reservation fee accordingly.

Action items: Priyom — please finalize the MAP acceptance checklist and mark the ramp month definition. Dev — flag if the SLA_credit_table needs any runtime caveats. Rishi — once checklist is ready, I'll ask legal to prepare an LOI and a short SOW for the reserved burst. Claire — if you confirm acceptance of those bullets, we'll circulate LOI by EOD next week.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial | Redwood Inference
(attachment: none)
